You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
an ecologist enthusiast
You are 30 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: a bachelor's degree. Your occupation: professional, scientific and technical services. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): a few times a week.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

We need to solve Othello endgame puzzle. We are Black (B). Need to pick move that maximizes final disc count assuming optimal opponent (White) play. The legal moves for Black: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. We need to compute outcome for each. The board state is given. Since we have limited time but can ask assistant. But we could also compute manually. However we have an AI assistant we can ask. But maybe we can just reason manually.

Yes. Empty: a1,h1,g2,a3,b6,a7,b7,a8,b8,c8 =10.

Legal moves for Black: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. Let's compute each.

In Othello, a legal move must outflank opponent discs in at least one direction.

- g2: placed at g2 (row2, col7). Adjacent squares: f2 is W, g1 is W, h2 is B. Let's see directions. From g2 to the right: h2 is B, so if any W between? There are none directly because h2 is immediate B. But direction left: f2 is W, e2 is B. So left direction outflanks f2 (W between g2 and e2). So flips f2. Direction up: g1 is W, but beyond g1 is nothing (off board) so no. Direction down: g3 is W, g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W. Beyond g8 off board, so no outflank downward. Diagonal ul: f1 is W, beyond f1 e0 offboard, no. Diagonal ur: h1 is ., no. Diagonal dl: f3 is W, e4 B -> outflanks f3? Wait from g2 down-left: f3 is W, e4 is B. Yes! So flipping f3. Down-right: h3 is B, immediate, no W between. Up-left: f1 is W, beyond offboard. Up-right: h1 . no. Down-left: f3 W, e4 B. So g2 flips f2 (left), f3 (down-left). Also maybe other directions? Let's check left: f2 W, e2 B. Yes. Down: g3 W, g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W, beyond offboard => no B beyond. So no. So g2 flips f2 and f3. That seems right.

- b6: placed at b6. Adjacent: a6 W, b5 B, b7 ., c6 B, a5 B, a7 ., c5 W, c7 W. Let's check directions: Up: b5 B immediate, no. Down: b7 . no. Left: a6 W, beyond a6? a6 is leftmost column, so no further. Wait left direction from b6 is a6, but to outflank you need a B beyond the W's. There's no square beyond a6. So no. Right: c6 B immediate. No. Up-left: a5 B immediate. No. Up-right: c5 W, d4 B! So diagonal up-right outflanks c5. So flips c5. Down-left: a7 . no. Down-right: c7 W, d8 W? Wait c7 is W, d8? Actually diagonal down-right from b6 goes to c7 (W), then d8 (W) then e9 offboard. Need a B beyond. No B in that line. So no. Down: b7 . no. Up: b5 B. Left: a6 W no beyond. So b6 flips c5 only?

Check also maybe horizontal left? a6 is W but no B beyond. So b6 only flips c5. Wait check diagonal down-left from b6: a7 empty. So no.

- a7: placed at a7. Adjacent: a6 W, b7 ., b8 ., b6 .? Actually b6 is row6 col2, from a7 up-right is b6 (.)? Wait a7 coordinates: row7 col1. Up: a6 W. Up-right: b6 . . Right: b7 . . Down-right: b8 . . Down: a8 . . Down-left: offboard. Left: offboard. Up-left: offboard. Need B beyond White. Up: a6 W, a5 B. So up direction outflanks a6. So flips a6. Any other? Right: b7 . no. Up-right: b6 . no. Down-right: b8 . no. So a7 flips a6 only.

- b7: placed at b7. Adjacent: a7 ., b6 ., b8 ., c7 W, a6 W, a8 ., c8 ., c6 B. Let's check directions. Left: a7 . no. Right: c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. So right direction outflanks c7,d7,e7,f7,g7. So flips all those 5. Up: b6 . no. Down: b8 . no. Up-left: a6 W, beyond a6? a6 is leftmost, no B beyond. Wait up-left from b7 goes to a6 (row6 col1). a6 is W. To outflank need a B beyond a6 in that direction, but offboard. So no. Up-right: c6 B immediate. No. Down-left: a8 . no. Down-right: c8 . no. So b7 flips c7-g7.

- b8: placed at b8. Adjacent: a8 ., b7 ., c8 ., a7 ., c7 W, a9 off, b9 off, c9 off, d9 off. Let's check. Actually from b8, up is b7 ., down offboard? Wait row8 is bottom, so down is offboard. Left a8 ., right c8 ., up-left a7 ., up-right c7 W, then d6 B? Let's trace: from b8 up-right: c7 W, d6 B. So up-right outflanks c7. So flips c7. Also maybe up: b7 . no. Right: c8 . no. Left: a8 . no. Down: offboard. Diagonal down-left offboard. Down-right offboard. Up-left a7 . no. So b8 flips c7 only? Wait maybe also horizontal? No.

- c8: placed at c8. Adjacent: b8 ., d8 W, c7 W, b7 ., d7 W, b9 off, d9 off, c9 off. Let's check. Left: b8 . no. Right: d8 W, e8 B. So right outflanks d8. Flips d8. Up: c7 W, c6 B. So up outflanks c7. Flips c7. Up-left: b7 . no. Up-right: d7 W, e6 B. So up-right outflanks d7. Flips d7. Down: offboard. Down-left offboard. Down-right offboard. Left-up etc. Also maybe diagonal left? No. So c8 flips d8, c7, d7.

So doesn't outflank. Down: a2 W. Down-right: b2 B immediate, but need W beyond? Actually need existing White beyond the Black line. From a1 down-right: b2 B, c3 B. Then d4 B... No W beyond. So no.

Wait direction right: c6 B, then d6 W. So yes, flips c6. Down: b7 . no. Down-right: c7 W immediate? Actually c7 is W, no. Up-left: a5 B, beyond a5? offboard? Wait up-left from b6 goes to a5 B, then offboard beyond. No W beyond. Up-right: c5 W immediate. No. Down-left: a7 . no. Down-right: c7 W immediate. So b6 for White flips b2,b3,b4,b5 (up) and c6 (right). That's 5 flips.

- a7: White at a7. Up: a6 W immediate, no. Right: b7 . no. Down: a8 . no. Down-right: b8 . no. Up-right: b6 . no. Diagonal up-left offboard. So not legal? Let's check if any Black line outflanked by existing White elsewhere. Could down-right from a7? b8 empty. No. So a7 not legal.

Left: a7 . no. Down-left: a8 . no. Down-right: c8 . no. So b7 is legal, flips c6 and d5.
